evidence.rootEvidenceAttributed: 440 (24 reader / 13 ledger integration / workspace) and 442 (5 capture / 24 reader / full security 404 passed 2 ignored / workspace). I reproduced the focused sets independently and replayed none of root's runs.

limits: Composition foundation only. No native capture adapter is rewired and no ACL or descriptor cost qualification follows; this review ran no ACL experiment.
The callback owes its own read and postcheck costs; arbitrary callback internals are not automatically bounded, and a pure calculator is not a reservation.

The runtime42 claim is the specific API one - new bytes and the pending outcome stay private until checks - not a general no-output authority; an arbitrary callback can still mutate captures or do external I/O.
No creator, P0 or current authority; no Linux, release, power-loss, full M2 or M2-M6 completion; existing law unchanged.
Root substantive assent and guarded private/live integration remain required.
observations: Zero slack is by design but leaves no headroom: because the calculation is exactly tight at growth boundaries, a caller reserving precisely read_bounded_cost(max, attempts) has nothing spare on that allowance. The docs point at checked_add for composition; worth knowing before sizing helpers are written.

attempts is unvalidated against the global cap, so a caller can compute a cost that can never be charged. The ledger refuses it before any callback, which is honest, but there is no early diagnostic separating an impossible reservation from an exhausted budget.

capture_accounted latches on the legacy-owned refusal. Consistent with the InvalidLimit pattern, but as at runtime40 and 42 a caller or configuration error closes the shared operation rather than reporting a distinguishable misuse.
The removed intermediate Arc is a correctness gain, not cleanup: it was an allocation that happened without being charged, so the change brings the ledger into line with what actually executes.
